key.answer_key: The O 1s spectrum resolves three oxygen-species components with distinct relative intensities: the Ce2O3 component is the tallest (~275), the Ce-OH component is next (~250), and the CeO2 component is the smallest (~100) (o21). This mix of Ce2O3, Ce-OH and CeO2 signals, rather than a single dominant, uniform CeO2 signature, is the panel reading that qualifies the thin/non-uniform, partial-coverage claim.
